description: Authored process-flow visualization paths for operator training. These are teaching overlays, not CFD or velocity/pressure simulation. Airflow is distributed across the measured side louver openings and fan outlet disks to communicate broad intake and full-diameter exhaust.

fanOpening.source: SolidWorks screenshot measurement from earlier fan-opening review

visualizationNotes.curveVisibility: air guide curves hidden; water guide curves lightly visible to clarify pipe/header routing
visualizationNotes.thermalColorGradient: air particles transition from cyan at louver intake to yellow through the cell and red-orange at the fan outlet to show heat absorbed from the water
visualizationNotes.mistPlumeBehavior: soft white translucent particles rise and expand above each fan outlet when Air Flow is active; teaching overlay only, not CFD or plume dispersion simulation
visualizationNotes.waterFlowBehavior: hot-water paths now use body-level anchors instead of broad group centers: filter vessel flange/body, 8-inch connector/valve/trunk, split branches, 5-inch valves, and individual riser tops; curves stay visible for tuning
visualizationNotes.waterRouteGranularity: body-level anchors with light visible guide curves
visualizationNotes.drainOverflowBehavior: Drain/overflow is authored as visible/front vertical takeoffs, local T merges, lower collector bends, and one common right-discharge collector so the overlay sits on the pipe centerline instead of between pipe faces.
